svg.text: ERA
PLACES YOU REMEMBER
SHEET 05 · TWELVE PLACES · VERSION 02
Not landmarks — gathering points. After twenty years here you would say “meet me there” with no address. Twelve places, one question each: why do people naturally stop here?
PRODUCTION CONCEPT · NOT FOR BUILD
same camera · locked architecture, voice, care and street language · no people, life implied
PL-01
THE BAKERY STEP
Q · bread comes out at seven; the step is warm
lit window before dawn · bench · two bikes · the crate
PL-02
THE OLD OAK
Q · you touch it before matches; it was here first
worn ring · scarves after wins · one bench, no design
PL-03
THE CORNER WALL
Q · it is exactly the height of sitting, and sees both streets
low brick wall · two bikes · a lamp for after dark
PL-04
THE BUS STOP AFTER SCHOOL
Q · everyone’s day starts and ends here
shelter · timetable · chalk on the flags · dropped bikes
PL-05
THE SHORTCUT
Q · it saves three minutes, and everyone knows
the gap between houses · worn line across the grass
PL-06
THE CAFÉ TERRACE
Q · you can see the whole street from a chair
three tables under the awning · the A-board promise
PL-07
OUTSIDE THE PUB
Q · the door faces the evening sun
two barrels on the flags · lantern · Friday implied
PL-08
THE SMALL BRIDGE
Q · the one place you may lean and do nothing
brick parapet · the stream · a bike left mid-errand
PL-09
THE NOTICE BOARD
Q · news lives here before it is news
parish board with its own roof · pillar box · three paths meet
PL-10
THE SQUARE
Q · Fridays it smells of flowers; other days it belongs to the kids
one stall, not a market · tree · chalk in the corner
PL-11
THE STADIUM PATH
Q · you walk it with everyone, every other Saturday
hedge one side, rail the other · a scarf on the fence · floodlights beyond
PL-12
THE DOCTOR’S GREEN
Q · you wait out here instead of inside
grass, one tree, two benches · the path everyone cuts
THE PLACE RULES
human scale; no monuments, no spectacle; every place is caused by everyday life; the ground remembers — worn paths are the town’s handwriting; football stays on the horizon.
SHEET 04 GAVE IT GROUND · SHEET 05 GIVES IT MEMORY
“let’s meet there” — and nobody asks where

LEAD’S VERDICT — strongest three: PL-01 THE BAKERY STEP (ritual — the day starts here, and the body remembers warmth and bread) · PL-08 THE SMALL BRIDGE (licensed idleness — the only place where stopping needs no excuse) · PL-02 THE OLD OAK (the only monument ERA allows: one that grew).

RECOMMENDED — THE OLD OAK as the emotional centre of every ERA town: it precedes the town; football touches it without owning it (scarves after wins); grief and celebration share it; and its meaning accumulates physically — the slowest clock of evidence-of-life.

WHY PEOPLE RETURN — each place pays in a different currency: bread for the body, idleness with permission, memory for belonging. None was designed to be beautiful; all were caused by life — which is why they become beautiful.
